title: Monochrome Press File — PDF/X-4 with a Gray output intent

metadata.author: pdfnative-cli samples
metadata.subject: PDF/X-4 (ISO 15930-7) under a Gray OutputIntent: one ink, /N 1, RGB remapped through /DefaultRGB (pdfnative 1.8.0)
metadata.keywords: print, pdf/x-4, output intent, gray, monochrome, prepress

outputIntent.info: A structurally valid, colourimetrically meaningless monochrome press profile shipped with the samples (gamma 2.2). Ask your printer for their ICC profile (e.g. Dot Gain 15 %).

blocks.text: pdfnative 1.8.0 accepts RGB, CMYK and Gray ICC profiles as the output intent and takes the component count (/N) from the profile itself. This file declares a Gray printing condition: a book interior, a form or a newspaper page printed in black only.

Rendered with --pdfx pdfx4 --output-intent-icc synthetic-gray.icc --trapped false --font latin --lang latin --strict. The profile is a 408-byte monochrome prtr profile generated by scripts/lib/synthetic-gray-profile.ts — valid, deterministic, and not a press condition.
What the engine does with colour

items: Device RGB content (this grey body text, the heading colour) is remapped through an inline calibrated /DefaultRGB colour space, so nothing on the page is device-dependent.
CMYK content would contradict a Gray intent: the render reports PDFX_DEVICE_CMYK, --strict refuses it, and inspect --check pdfx fails the file. This document uses none.
The printer's marks sit in a 3 mm bleed (8.5 pt): crop marks and registration targets are re-centred and thinned so they stay inside the MediaBox.

blocks.text: pdfnative inspect --input 06-gray-pdfx4.pdf --check pdfx exits 0; pdfnative inspect --pdfx prints the validator's errors and warnings.
